jobs.description:
Executive Director of External Relations and Engagement (0457U), School of Social Welfare \#88417 About Berkeley
  
  

At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  

Departmental Overview
  
  

Berkeley Social Welfare is one of the nation's leading social work graduate programs. As part of the world's top ranked public university, the School of Social Welfare is producing new knowledge for the common good and training the next generation of social work thought leaders dedicated to serving society's most vulnerable members. Known for combining rigorous scholarship with outstanding education, the School of Social Welfare offers MSW and PhD programs as well as an undergraduate major. Since 1944, the School has prepared nearly 12,000 social work professionals for leadership positions in the public and nonprofit human service sectors. Berkeley Social Welfare graduates are dedicated to meeting the growing needs of marginalized, underserved and other vulnerable populations.
  
  

This position will assist the Dean in developing new strategic initiatives in education and scholarship. It is modeled after those held by academic program managers in federally sponsored research centers, and in some academic departments, but encompasses the additional complexity of being required to develop a significantly broader network of sponsors from agencies and other external organizations, in addition to academic institutions. Another element of this position will be translating the interests of these various partners and stakeholders into outreach, research and learning activities that engage Social Welfare faculty and students. This position supports the development of a range of scholarly and educational initiatives, including undergraduate and graduate courses, certificate programs, a range of professional education options including executive education as well as new domains for inter\-professional knowledge building.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

The Executive Director of External Relations and Engagement is responsible for providing strategic leadership and operational management across the school's external engagement functions, including communications, fundraising, revenue\-generating programs, events and alumni relations, research development, and instructional technology and design. In addition to managing and developing a team of direct reports, the Executive Director will perform short and long range planning, conduct market research, leverage data to identify and propose new initiatives and revenue streams, and, as needed, liaise with relevant campus departments and external partners to accomplish goals.
  
  

The Executive Director works closely with the Dean/Associate Dean, a faculty committee focused on revenue generation, and other administrative leaders and is responsible for ensuring goals are on track and met, and may propose high\-level recommendations for improvements and/or changes to enhance the School's external engagement and revenue.
  
  

Application Review Date
  
  

The First Review Date for this job is September 28, 2026\. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  

Responsibilities
  
  

External Engagement Strategy and Infrastructure
  
  

Acts as key thought partner to the Dean and Senate Faculty on the conception, implementation, management, and scaling of innovative initiatives that involve senior management, faculty, and external stakeholders to extend and enhance the School's reputation and impact.
  
  

Administratively directs initiatives with high autonomy upon approval from the Dean and Senate Faculty, ensuring alignment with School and University goals and policies.
  
Develops business plans, budgets, and KPIs; assesses and reports on initiative effectiveness and recommends structural or procedural changes to optimize results for assigned programs.
  
Leads the rebuild of the development and external engagement function.
  
  

Represents School, in coordination with or in lieu of the Dean, Senate Faculty, and other members of the School, to a network of partners, sponsors, government agencies, multilateral organizations, peer programs, foundations, private donors, alumni, and the public to cultivate and steward relationships with the key research and capacity building partners.
  
  

Creates and manages a unified platform for existing and potential community partnerships across government, industry, foundations, and non\-profit sectors in Airtable.
  
Identifies and cultivates new opportunities for collaboration with peer institutions, research centers and groups, and public and private sector partners that advance the educational and research priorities of the school.
  
Develops scopes of work, pitches, and budgets for new programs, working closely with finance offices and funders to secure necessary resources.

**About Little Rangers**

Little Rangers is Nature Rangers Wilderness Programs' outdoor early childhood program, created to give young children the kind of childhood they thrive in: hands on, imaginative, active, connected, and full of discovery.

Our days happen outdoors and are designed around the way young children naturally learn best: through movement, play, sensory experiences, curiosity, relationships, and real world exploration. **The goal is to support each child’s development at a natural, individual pace, while creating the conditions where they can grow into confident, curious, resilient little people.**

We are looking for a Director who can bring a strong understanding of early childhood development into the heart of the Nature Rangers approach, while keeping the experience joyful, creative, playful, and unmistakably fun.

**The Opportunity**

Nature Rangers Wilderness Programs is seeking an exceptional **Little Rangers Director** to lead and continue developing our early childhood outdoor education program.

We're looking for more than someone who enjoys working with children. The right person genuinely **understands children**.

You know how young children's brains develop and what they need socially, emotionally, physically, cognitively, and creatively. You understand developmental milestones, but you also know that children don't all arrive at them in exactly the same way or on exactly the same timetable.

You know how to meet children where they are, recognize what they may be ready for next, and create experiences that gently encourage them to stretch, explore, problem solve, connect, and grow.

You are also highly creative. You can look at a trail, a pile of sticks, a patch of dirt, or a rainy morning and immediately start imagining what children could do with it.

Most importantly, you love being with young children and believe childhood should include movement, imagination, laughter, healthy challenges, connection, dirt, wonder, and a lot of time outside.

* Has a strong working knowledge of early childhood development and how young children think, learn, communicate, regulate, connect, and grow.
* Genuinely enjoys working with toddlers and preschool aged children.
* Understands developmental milestones and knows how to help children work toward and beyond them in age appropriate, encouraging ways.
* Can recognize the individual needs of a child and adjust activities, communication, expectations, and support accordingly.
* Is **creative, imaginative, playful, and resourceful**.
* Brings original ideas for activities, games, stories, projects, sensory experiences, and outdoor adventures.
* Takes initiative and is comfortable taking ownership of a program.
* Is collaborative and excited to develop curriculum and programming alongside the Executive Director.
* Has a deep appreciation for nature, outdoor education, and experiential learning.
* Can thoughtfully adapt the established **Nature Rangers philosophy and style** to the developmental needs of younger children.
* Is warm, patient, energetic, observant, dependable, and emotionally attuned.
* Believes in helping children build **Confidence, Curiosity, and Resilience**.

**Key Responsibilities**

The Little Rangers Director will take a leadership role in both the daily experience of the children and the continued development of the program.

Responsibilities include:

* Create a welcoming, joyful, developmentally appropriate outdoor environment for young children.

jobs.title: Executive Vice President, Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**About Hall Equities Group**

Hall Equities Group is a private, full\-service real estate investment, development, and property management company representing the interests of select private investors and company\-sponsored group investment entities. The company organizes and manages investment opportunities on behalf of its partners, their families, its shareholders, and key employees. With over fifty years of experience in the real estate industry, Hall Equities Group has demonstrated proficiency across multiple property types, including industrial, multi\-family housing, retail shopping centers, branded and boutique hotels, office buildings, self\-storage, sports training facilities, subdivisions, and master planned communities.

Hall Equities Group operates as part of a broader, affiliated business ecosystem that includes ZMC Hotels, COPA Innovation Laboratories, National SportsMall Realty, and several additional businesses spanning real estate, hospitality, sports, technology, and innovation. While each business operates with its own focus, the interconnected ecosystem benefits from a centralized leadership and shared services model seated in Hall Equities Group.

**Position Overview**

The Executive Vice President/COO of Hall Equities Group is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the day\-to\-day operations and financial performance of the company’s diverse commercial real estate portfolio, spanning a broad range of asset classes including multifamily, retail, office, industrial, medical, self\-storage, master\-planned communities, athletic complexes, and hospitality. Reporting directly to the CEO, this position provides strategic and operational oversight across property management, financial performance, budgeting, leasing, capital expenditures, third\-party ownership relationships, and property\-level legal and operational matters.

This role serves as a central point of accountability across the portfolio, ensuring portfolio asset managers, property managers, and supporting teams are operating effectively, financial information is accurate and timely, leasing activity is aligned with forecasts, capital projects are properly managed, and property\-level issues are identified and addressed proactively. The position requires a hands\-on leader who can manage both people and processes while maintaining a comprehensive understanding of the performance of each property.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Property Management \& Portfolio Operations**

* Provide overall leadership and oversight of property management operations across the Hall Equities Group portfolio.
* Manage and support the day\-to\-day activities of the property management team, establishing clear expectations, priorities, and accountability.
* Review property operations regularly to ensure properties are being managed efficiently, professionally, and in accordance with ownership objectives.
* Identify operational issues, risks, and opportunities across the portfolio and work with property managers and leadership to develop solutions.
* Establish and maintain consistent operating standards, processes, and reporting across properties.
* Review the work product and performance of property management personnel and ensure deadlines, reporting requirements, and operational responsibilities are being met.
* Serve as an escalation point for significant tenant, vendor, operational, or property\-level issues.

**Financial Oversight \& Reporting**

* Lead and oversee the annual budgeting process across the real estate portfolio.
* Review monthly property financial statements, cash balances, operating results, and supporting financial information for accuracy and completeness.
* Confirm that financial performance is consistent with approved budgets and identify significant variances or emerging issues.
* Prepare, review, and coordinate quarterly property and portfolio narratives for executive leadership and shareholders.
* Maintain visibility into the financial position and operating performance of each property.
* Work closely with accounting, property management, and executive leadership to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting.
* Review accounts payable activity as appropriate and provide oversight of property\-level expenses and payment processes.

**Team Leadership \& Personnel Management**

* Provide direct management and leadership to property management personnel and supporting operations staff.
* Establish priorities, monitor performance, and ensure accountability across the operations team.
* Conduct regular reviews of workload, property assignments, staffing requirements, and team performance.
* Participate in and approve the hiring process for new property management and operations personnel.
* Support onboarding, training, professional development, and performance management.
* Help establish scalable operating procedures and organizational structures as the portfolio evolves.

Legal Aid at Work (LAAW) partners with people to help them understand and assert their workplace rights, and advocates for employment laws and systems that empower low\-paid workers and marginalized communities.

Fully Virtual \| $75,000–$80,000 \| National Scope

About FairWays to Leadership

FairWays to Leadership (FWTL) is a 501(c)(3\) leadership development organization built on a distinctive premise: golf can be both a classroom for leadership and a doorway into professional relationships and opportunities. Founded in 2020, FWTL introduces college students, many of whom have had little or no previous exposure to golf, to the game while helping them build the confidence, leadership capabilities, professional language, and relationships that can broaden their access to opportunity.

FWTL’s mission is to promote access to leaders and leadership opportunities through golf literacy. Its immersive six\-week program intentionally connects the experience of learning golf with the development of six leadership traits: adaptability, mindfulness, integrity, curiosity, empowerment, and strategy. Students participate in leadership learning and on\-course instruction, using real moments in the game to practice judgment, self\-awareness, resilience, relationship building, and strategic thinking.

The goal is not simply to create more golfers. FWTL equips emerging leaders with enough fluency in the game, confidence on the course, and understanding of golf’s role in business culture to participate in professional spaces that may once have felt unfamiliar or inaccessible. Through its curriculum, Executive Forum, university relationships, golf\-industry partners, and growing alumni network, FWTL helps students connect what they learn on the course to how they lead, network, and pursue opportunities beyond it.

FWTL now has a strong programmatic foundation, an engaged Board of Directors, committed partners, and a growing alumni community. The organization is entering a pivotal next phase: expanding its reach while building the revenue, partnerships, staff capacity, systems, and infrastructure required for sustainable growth.

We Are Looking for a Builder and a Fundraiser

The next Executive Director will be responsible not only for leading FairWays to Leadership, but for building a sustainable nonprofit that serves students on a national level. The defining requirement for this role is a demonstrated record of growing organizations and raising the funds needed to sustain that growth.

This is a highly external leadership role. The successful candidate will build and personally steward relationships with corporate sponsors, foundations, major donors, university partners, golf\-industry leaders, and other champions of the mission. They will turn those relationships into a stronger and more diversified revenue base, while working with the Board to make disciplined choices about where and how FWTL expands.

The right leader will be equally comfortable setting direction and rolling up their sleeves. In a small, growth\-stage organization, strategy and execution are closely connected. Executive Director, FairWays to Leadership

FairWays to Leadership Seeks an Executive Director to Lead Its Next Phase of Growth

Fully Virtual \| $75,000–$80,000 \| National Scope

About FairWays to Leadership

FairWays to Leadership (FWTL) is a 501(c)(3\) leadership development organization built on a distinctive premise: golf can be both a classroom for leadership and a doorway into professional relationships and opportunities. Founded in 2020, FWTL introduces college students, many of whom have had little or no previous exposure to golf, to the game while helping them build the confidence, leadership capabilities, professional language, and relationships that can broaden their access to opportunity.

FWTL’s mission is to promote access to leaders and leadership opportunities through golf literacy. Its immersive six\-week program intentionally connects the experience of learning golf with the development of six leadership traits: adaptability, mindfulness, integrity, curiosity, empowerment, and strategy. Students participate in leadership learning and on\-course instruction, using real moments in the game to practice judgment, self\-awareness, resilience, relationship building, and strategic thinking.

The goal is not simply to create more golfers. FWTL equips emerging leaders with enough fluency in the game, confidence on the course, and understanding of golf’s role in business culture to participate in professional spaces that may once have felt unfamiliar or inaccessible. Through its curriculum, Executive Forum, university relationships, golf\-industry partners, and growing alumni network, FWTL helps students connect what they learn on the course to how they lead, network, and pursue opportunities beyond it.

FWTL now has a strong programmatic foundation, an engaged Board of Directors, committed partners, and a growing alumni community. The organization is entering a pivotal next phase: expanding its reach while building the revenue, partnerships, staff capacity, systems, and infrastructure required for sustainable growth.

We Are Looking for a Builder and a Fundraiser

The defining requirement for this role is a demonstrated record of growing organizations and raising the funds needed to sustain that growth.

This is a highly external leadership role. The successful candidate will build and personally steward relationships with corporate sponsors, foundations, major donors, university partners, golf\-industry leaders, and other champions of the mission. They will turn those relationships into a stronger and more diversified revenue base, while working with the Board to make disciplined choices about where and how FWTL expands.

The right leader will be equally comfortable setting direction and rolling up their sleeves. In a small, growth\-stage organization, strategy and execution are closely connected. The Executive Director must be able to articulate an ambitious vision, build the case for investment, close funding commitments, strengthen organizational systems, support staff, and ensure that program quality remains high as the organization scales.

Assists the Director of Global Security in developing, implementing, and administering Land O’Lakes’ enterprise\-wide global security strategy and program. This role supports the development and advocacy of security policies, standards, and operational risk reduction measures to reduce vulnerabilities and limit exposure. A key focus is strengthening the existing global investigative program to mitigate procedural and technical risks while protecting people, assets, and reputation in alignment with Land O’Lakes policies, procedures, and culture.

* Serve as the liaison to law enforcement and other governmental agencies related to safety and security.
